newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Friday were inactive with bids at $62.00, unchanged from Thursday's moderate sales, passed by owners pricing cattle at $63.00 to $65.00, cattle feeders said.
Fed cattle prices were underpinned by strong packer demand this week which depleted showlists in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and most in Kansas, they said.
Active packer buying was tied to firm retail beef demand for planned beef features in mid- to late July and early August, market sources said.

Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by steep advances Thursday in CME live cattle futures and the ability of feedlots to remain current, especially in the Texas Panhandle area, as indicated by this week's cattle sales, sources said.

Packers now have enough cattle to get through next week and there were even reports of some sales Thursday that had one to two extra days, instead of the normal seven, attached to them, several feedlot sources said.
Cattle owners were said to be anticipating further strength next week and were seen pricing cattle at $65.00, they said.
